utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Madam Registrar. If you could kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record, all the accused are here. Amongst the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Bourgon, and Mr. Haynes. Prosecution is represented by Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey had a doctor's appointment that was essential this morning. He will join us as soon as he's through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you for that information, Mr. Thayer. So I see on my screen our representative of the registrar, Ms. Yaiza Alvarez Reyes, flanked to her right by a gentleman who I take it is the witness. I am also informed that there is a magistrate present and a legal officer. Perhaps they could identify themselves for the record before we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Magistrate, unfortunately your name did not register. If you could repeat it, please, sir. MAGISTRATE (redacted): I said, Your Honour, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much and good -- in your case it would be good evening. So it's -- MAGISTRATE (redacted): I beg your pardon. I have to address a technical problem [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. It is 9.15 in the morning here on the 5th of September. Before I address the witness directly I wish to inform him as to who is present in this courtroom and what measures we have taken or put in place for the purpose of the protective measures that we granted some time back. I am the Presiding Judge and my name is Carmel Agius. I am flanked on my right by Judge O-Gon Kwon and to my left by Judge Kim Prost. On my extreme right we have Judge Ole Bjorn Stole, who is reserve Judge in this case. Then of course there are the seven accused here, and if at any time the witness wishes to know their names, I will give him the information. They are each assisted by a team of lawyers, and then for the Prosecution there is only one gentleman present with his -- assisted by his case manager. The lead counsel will be showing up later on, because as stated he's got a medical appointment this morning. The rest are legal and clerical staff of this Tribunal. Now, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are going to start giving evidence in a few minutes, and before you do so, I need to explain to you that our rules require you to make a solemn declaration to the effect that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is going to be handed to you now by Madam Registrar. Please read it out aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that will be your -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You would be aware that we have put in place for you some protective measures, namely the use of a pseudonym instead of using your real name. You will be known here and in the records as PW-100. We have also put in place face and voice distortion. Let me explain --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been informed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me explain to you how this is going to work. One moment, because we have a technical problem here. Now, let me explain to you what's going to happen. We were informed by our technical man here that direct reception via videolink as it is happening now would not transmit your image or your voice in a distorted manner, so inside the courtroom, inside the four walls of the courtroom, we can see you and we can hear you. That's nothing special, because whenever a witness comes to testify live with the same protective measures here in The Hague those who are present inside the courtroom can see him or her and can hear his or her voice. What's important is that we have ensured that outside the four walls of this courtroom the transmission to the public takes place with the protective measures in place, namely your visual appearance and your voice are already being distorted. We have also taken an extraordinary measure to ensure that the application of these protective measures is full; namely, that since we usually get quite an audience in the gallery, and in this case anyone sitting in the public gallery could see the screens or the monitors that are available to most of counsel here in the courtroom, we have closed down the courtroom curtains so that anyone who may be in the public gallery cannot have a visual view of the courtroom itself or any of the monitors. I want an assurance from you that this is to your satisfaction, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So what's going to happen now is Mr. Thayer is going to ask you a series of questions, an examination-in-chief. He will then be followed by some or all of the Defence teams on cross-examination. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I proceed, I think a caution pursuant to Rule 90(E) would be in order and I believe that's already been explained to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Thayer. Witness, we've been asked to draw your attention to a special provision of our rules explaining -- laying down and explaining a right that you have which at the outset I must tell you is not an absolute right. Now, in the course of the examination-in-chief or cross-examinations, you may be asked questions which if answered truthfully could potentially expose you to future criminal proceedings. I'm not saying that there will be such questions, but I cannot exclude them either. My duty is to alert you to a right which our rules protect, namely the right against self-incrimination of a witness. Should there be any such questions and you wish not to answer such questions because they are incriminatory ones, then you can address us, the Judges here, and ask for an exemption. We may decide to grant you an exemption or we may decide exactly the opposite. And this is why your right is not absolute. If we exempt you then of course we will move on to the next question and you won't answer the incriminatory one. If we compel you to answer such so-called incriminatory questions then you enjoy a further right under our rules, namely that unless your answer to such questions constitutes false testimony, then whatever you state in answering such questions would not be used and could not be used against you in any future criminal that proceedings. Have you understood my explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So I think, Mr. Thayer, we can now safely proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning to you and to Your Honours. Good morning everyone up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, good morning to you. Good morning to Madam Registrar. And good morning, Your Worship. Sir, we haven't met or even -- MAGISTRATE (redacted): I beg your pardon. I have to address a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Worship. MAGISTRATE (redacted): Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. The technical difficulty was [indiscernible] recording, a difficulty with the recording equipment [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I take it we're ready to proceed? MAGISTRATE (redacted): Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, Madam Registrar will be shortly handing you a piece of paper. I would ask you simply to read the paper to yourself and please confirm that your name is written next to the pseudonym PW-100.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Again, we've not met or spoken. We're just going to basically have a conversation this morning. I'm going to take you very carefully and chronologically through these events. I would just ask you to please, especially with all the technical hookups we've got and the interpretation, please take your time, listen carefully to the entire question no matter who's asking the question, and take your time in answering. If you don't understand any part of a question anyone asks you, please just say so. If you need a break at any time, again please just say so. And you may see me from time to time looking away, looking down. I'm not being rude. I'm just checking my monitor to see that the transcript is accurate or looking at the exhibits. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may we enter private session for a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, just bearing in mind Mr. President's caution about any information that might disclose your identity, would you please just take us through what happened, how you got from Janja to wherever your destination was in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In the buses. The buses had taken us to -- to the final destination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Bosnia do you know what authority was taking control or custody of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In the beginning we believed it was reserve police force, and then the following day we had realised that actually it has been a special police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where exactly were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To Jahorina [indiscernible] time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there a particular facility where you were taken to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I believe it was called hotel Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court approximately how many men in your similar circumstances were brought down with you to the Jahorina hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say about 300 to 350.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you arrived at this location what were you told was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Nothing, just training. In the beginning before we had been transferred to Jahorina we'd been told that actually we're just going to be doing the guarding, like guarding duties of the municipalities and -- and nothing, nothing combat way type of duty to be concerned at all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask you to make a brief pause between questions and answers, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Our attention has been drawn by the interpreters that they are encountering some problems. They would kindly ask you to allow for a brief pause between question and answer since you both speak the same language. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, was there anyone in particular in charge of this training that you just referred to a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. There was a gentleman by the name of Dusko Jevic in control of facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'll ask you some more questions about him in a little while, but while you were there, that is after your first day of arrival, were there other busloads of men in your similar circumstances arriving or did they all arrive in one batch with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say that there had been few batches of buses coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would that have resulted in the total of approximately 300 to 350 men that you mentioned before, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you free to leave this -- this area or this facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point were you issued any uniform or -- or equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you please describe that for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We just had been -- one morning, I believe it was second morning, we had been just lined up and given the uniform, and couple of days after that we had been given the personal weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe the uniform? How was it designed? What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Two-piece camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what kind of weapon were you issued, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say it's automatic rifle which probably NATO would be AK47.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you issued any protective gear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was that, sir, and would you describe it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was a bullet-proof vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what colour it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. It was light blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you remember the quality of that -- that vest, sir, the quality of the construction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was too great. It was poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to ask you a few questions about the structure and organisation of yourself and the other men that were brought down to Jahorina. From now on, sir, I'll just refer to them as recruits, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber how you and your fellow recruits were organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We have been split in half like two divisions with further split of every half into the four units and each of unit has been split in a further four smaller units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You referred to two divisions. Did those divisions have a name, platoon, company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't remember this at this present in time, but it was -- I believe it was Company 1, Company 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember the name of the person who commanded the 1st company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: The 1st company, I believe his name was Mane.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall at all what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Dark hair, medium -- medium to -- to larger build, strong. I would say mid-30s then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. And -- I'm sorry, I didn't know if you were finished with your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I'm finished with my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about the commander of the 2nd Company? Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: His name was Nedzo Ikonic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you offer any type of description for Mr. Ikonic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: A similar height like Mane. He was not as built as Mane. He was slightly slimmer. Dark hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that the two companies were then subdivided into four other units. Those four other units, can you recall approximately how many men were in each of those four units, and if you remember the name of -- that was given to those units, that would also be helpful.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you, I can't remember now but if -- if you wouldn't mind if I could look up the statement that I have given before so I can refresh my memory a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. We can do that, and that is your OTP witness statement at page 5, and it is also page 5 of the B/C/S version. I think you'll find the information there, and I'll just let you read it and let us know when -- when and if your memory has been refreshed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know we are not privy to prior witness statements to the OTP or to others except that we get an indication that they exist? I have here two witness statements purportedly made by the witness. One goes to the 12th of December and the other one to the 18th of December, both 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the OTP witness statement that began 14 December and ended in 18 December as opposed to the statement to the UNHCR which was taken earlier that month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Could you verify also with the witness the ERN number of the page that you just pointed out to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. That is ERN 00363825.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That -- Mr. Thayer, that doesn't correspond with what we have here. If it's the 18th December 1995 OTP witness statement that you are referring to, the B/C/S ERN is 0307 -- starts at 03074399 and ends with 4418, and the English ERN 1499649 to 9672. We want the witness to know that it's not the practice of this Trial Chamber at least to have available prior witness out-of-court statements, so we need, however, to be able to know precisely what he is reading and what he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I mean, we're proceeding this way. If he had been here I would have handed it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's one further reason why we need to inquire and make sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- which document he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [] Your Honour, I can assist. The document provided to the witness in English, witness statement ERN 01499649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And which page, Yaiza, is he reading?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [] He's reading the English version, page number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page number 6. All right. That would help you focus better, Mr. Thayer, and your -- the other Defence counsels, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, have you had an opportunity to review that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And let me just repeat the question I asked previously. Do you remember the generic name of the individual units that the companies were subdivided into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I cannot recall any generic name of the unit, but, yeah, it was Company 1 and Company 2, and we had four platoons per company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recall the names of any of the platoon leaders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In Company 1 platoon 1, Nedzo. That is the first name, but I don't think it's the same person as the -- the Company 2 leader. It's Company 1 platoon 2 Tomo, company 1 platoon 3 Nedzo again and company 1 platoon 4 is Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You've mentioned three Nedzos so far today. The second Nedzo who you mentioned was a platoon leader, is that the same Nedzo as Nedzo Ikonic or is it a different Nedzo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We had different Nedzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And within each of the platoons you indicated that they were subdivided into four smaller units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- one moment yes Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record I would like to identify that witness is literally reading his statement out. This is what I can see. If the witness cannot remember, that's all right for him to look at it and refresh his memory, but reading his previous statement, it's meaningless. I mean, I don't see the point of this kind of examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Do you wish to comment on that Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, having -- Mr. President, I'll ask him if he's refreshed his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, or perhaps you can deal directly with on this point with the witness who should know that he should be giving testimony live and not reading from his previous statement. He may refer to it, of course, if he needs to refresh his memory, but then his testimony should be testimony and not reading out from the -- from the previous statement. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you were -- you were furnished with a copy of your OTP witness statement and you obviously had an opportunity to review it. Having reviewed it, do you have an independent recollection of the names of those platoon leaders without having to actually sit down and look at it while you're answering the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you it has happened 12 years ago so, yeah, now if I'm more aware I would be able to tell the names without looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. But the question is did reviewing that statement refresh your recollection and enable you to answer the question without having to read the document as you are answering the question? In other words, could you answer the question now without making reference to the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. One moment, Mr. Thayer. For the record lead counsel for the Prosecution Mr. McCloskey has entered the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I don't know if that satisfies my friend. I mean, I can ask him to answer the question again but I think we've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness has understood precisely what the point was and we can proceed. He can refresh his memory any time this becomes necessary, but then his testimony should -- should not be reading out from the previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, within the smallest unit, that is the units within each platoon, did those lowest-level units have somebody that was a leader of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not really. It was a one person out of lowest level that actually was a person, not a leader in a grade state, but that was the person, like a spokesperson of that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who appointed that lowest-level spokesperson, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: The leaders of the platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that lowest-level spokesperson, was he somebody like yourself and your fellow recruits or was he is somebody who was a regular special police brigade member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would -- I would say it was the same person recruit that how -- appeared to be that he wore the same uniform. Everything was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, as for the platoons and the platoon leaders, you just mentioned, I believe, four names. Were those platoon leaders recruits like yourselves or regular special police brigade members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: They would be regular special -- they would be regular members.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which platoon were you in, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who actually conducted your training? Who oversaw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was overseen by the -- by the platoon leaders and by the company leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And by the way, sir, do you recall the names of any of the platoon leaders for the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe this training that you received. How long did it last, and what did it consist in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In the beginning it was purely fitness training, and then after we did receive the training to get handle with the personal weapon, bits and pieces of training with the mines, bits and -- we had the shootings as well in target shooting, bits and pieces like in the hostage situation, reacting of the hostage situation, like in the real life the proper police -- a special police force member how would react in a hostage situation, and we did -- had a brief training on -- with rocket-propelled grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during this period of -- of training, other than your training officers, these platoon leaders and the -- the other regular special police brigade members, the company leaders that you described, did you see other regular special police brigade members in that area of Jahorina where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. They used to be -- usually there is a -- there are other facilities on -- on a close vicinity, different hotels that served in a different purpose. I believe there was another station of the regular Special Police Unit in Jahorina in different hotel and there was a hotel for, I would say, politicians or -- we were not allowed to go into these hotels.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you and your fellow recruits treated any differently by the superior officers at this Jahorina facility than the regular special police brigade members were treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Definitely, yes. We have been mistrusted, been called deserters, and were not allowed, actually, to move any further. We could not enter these other two facilities. We would only be able to enter the facility where we have been in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned Dusko Jevic some time ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just share any recollections you have of him during this period of time with the Trial Chamber? What do you remember about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In which sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Any sense is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Can you please clarify the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. First of all, anything about his attitude, anything about the way he trained you, anything he said or did that stands out in your mind in particular. Let's start there first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay. In the beginning he gave us a lecture how he's a soldier and how every single soldier should be behaving in the combat and especially when there is a prisoner of war that should be held and kept under Geneva Convention and that there is no harm to be done to them under no circumstances. If there is any mistreatment to be done to them, those fighters are becoming more fierce fighters if they get exchanged, and they take the arms on the other side, and that's -- that's pretty much it. And sometimes he would -- it was -- it was pretty much contradictory person. Sometimes he would be saying things like that and sometimes he would come to us and say, like, to kill a person is not a big deal. It just -- you know, you should kill one to see how not -- it's not hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you anything about what to do in terms of killing a prisoner of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: If -- if prisoner of war had to be killed it should be done in a military way with the bullet and not with any other different type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember anything in particular about his appearance, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In -- in which sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about his physical appearance that stands out in your mind? If not, that's okay. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Physical appearance like physical description of him or --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure. We'll start there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was -- it was not -- not tall. He was not tall, dark hair, moustaches, slim build. Looks like -- did look like Joseph Stalin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in fact was he known by any particular nickname, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we had learned later on, that actually his nickname was "Stalin."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to move into a new area now. Did you receive an order at some time to leave Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Before we -- we have been shifted to the area of Potocari, no, but when we have got the order, we had the alert, and we had quick assembly and we had been informed that we are leaving for Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who do you recall issuing that order to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: When we have been assembled Mr. Jevic was there with somebody who was of highest rank to him, and I did see that person briefly, and that was just quick -- quick short statement and off you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At that time, sir, before you departed were you told anything about what your assignment was going to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, before you departed what information, if any, did you have about the progress of the military assault on the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We had no information at all, absolutely nothing. We didn't know what was going to happen to us. We were just -- didn't have any information, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So how did you actually leave Jahorina, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: If I can recall properly, on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who actually left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: All -- all -- all conscripts or how you're going to call them. Everybody left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Only -- only handful -- only handful of injured people or who had medical problems had been left behind, but I would say everybody left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And forgive me if you've already answered this question. I know you told us which platoon you were in, but which company were you in, sir, and who was -- who was your company commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you leave the same day that you received this order, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We ended up in school, if I could recall properly. We ended up in a school near -- in the close vicinity. I really didn't know where -- where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mentioned in the close vicinity. In the close vicinity of what location, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Probably in close vicinity of Potocari or Bratunac, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: All I remember it was -- all I remember, it was near Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And by any chance do you remember the village in which the school was located, and if you don't, that's okay, we can just move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't recall that name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of the day you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say it was late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you arrived there do you recall whether there were any other units of the regular special police brigade or just ordinary police officers or the army billeted at that same location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I could not recall any of them. It was only us from Jahorina camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you spend the first night there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to ask you some questions now about the next day. What was your assignment that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Our assignment that day was to go to Potocari and to secure perimeters. We had been informed that the problems are not expected and that we are just there to secure the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what the -- the jump-off point was from where you started to head into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was close to the UN post before Potocari, on the road. I don't recall the particular point, but it was not very close to Potocari. It was the UN post. It was actually the Dutch post that was there on road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did (redacted) or any other officer tell you anything more, number one, what to expect when you reached Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We have been told that there are going to be civilians, that they're going to be shipped to Tuzla or exchanged, and there is no problems to be expected. There won't be any problems there. And our task there is to make sure that no federal army, if there is any members left, can come in and hurt anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to departing for this check-point, sir, or prior to setting out towards Potocari what, if anything, were you told about what your role, that is your fellow Jahorina members' role would be, if anything, with respect to the civilians in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I can't recall any, any particular orders apart of making sure that everything goes okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say making sure everything goes okay, what are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That there is no problem, actually to make sure that the civilians are all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your understanding as to what was going to happen to the civilians, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: My understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer the question. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness already explained what his actual task was. Everything in the last three questions, I don't see -- I believe that this question is just repeating the previous ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the previous questions were -- and answers, in particular, were rather broad and to an extent vague. In answering this last question, he would probably clarify at least his understanding of the order received.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure. What was your understanding as to the role that you and your fellow Jahorina members were supposed to take with respect to these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To make sure that the civilians are not hurt and to -- to protect them from any -- any possible attack from the federal army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And my understanding was that they're going to all be shipped to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. There's one part I don't understand. First what he understands by the federal army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then depending on his answer I will consider putting a second one. Which was the federal army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, your understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is that is the army that is Croatia and Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And why would the BiH army, then -- the federation did not exist as yet. Why would the BiH army, as distinguished from the VRS army, want to -- or wish to harm Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably some provoking attack or something like that. Just it was made clear to us that we need to protect the civilians, if anybody basically comes in shooting, to shoot back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, sir, your understanding was that the civilians, Muslim civilians, needed to be protected from any possible provocative attack by the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It also occurred to you that they could also be the subject of attacks from the -- by the VRS, and was it your understanding that you were there to protect them from that too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. At no point it was said that perhaps VRS or any -- any part of any arm of Republika Srpska is going to do any harm to the civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what was your understanding as to the role that you and your fellow Jahorina members were to take with respect to the transportation or evacuation of these civilians to Tuzla, as you had just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. This is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We have an objection. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that was a very, very leading question. It already suggests that his unit had some tasks in respect to the transport or evacuation. He was asked what was his understanding of the task of his unit. He answered that. There is no -- he never suggested they had anything to do with the evacuation or transportation. Now this question is a very leading one. My colleague is literally putting words into the mouth of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If anything, the question itself lends itself to misinterpretation basically because I don't necessarily read it to mean that the Jahorina members, including the witness, were tasked with the transportation or evacuation of the civilians. The way I understand it at least is knowing that there was going to be or you were told that there was going to be a transportation or evacuation of those civilians to Tuzla, what was your role?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In that respect, if any, yes. That's how I read the question. Although as it is as you put it I think it could lend itself to the way Mr. Lazarevic understood it. So now I think I've made it clear and if that is what you had in mind asking the witness then the witness can proceed to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was precisely what I was trying to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you both, Mr. Thayer and Mr. Lazarevic. Witness, perhaps now you can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think -- I never thought that we going to be doing anything with the transportation. My belief was when I got there and with the point when I have been posted that actually just stand there because we really didn't know what are we doing there simply because we've been told we're going to secure the premises to make sure nothing happens to civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I just want to ask you one or two more questions on this topic before we move on. Do you remember what you told the OTP investigators on this topic when you met with them in December of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Would you mind if I look it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not at all, sir. I can direct your attention to your OTP witness statement, the same one that we mentioned before at page 7. In English the ERN is 01499655, and it's the paragraph that begins: "The next morning we were assigned to reach the Dutch compound." And for my friends following in B/C/S, I believe that is also page 7, and it is the top of the page, and this ERN is 03074405. Do you see where it says: "Our mission was to prevent the Muslim fighters from entering the area and we were also to take in charge the evacuation of the civilians"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My question, sir, is, number one, do you recall saying that to the investigators in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: When I see this on a statement, and back then in 1995 it was closer to the event, I would -- I would say I did say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the second question related to that, sir: Is that an accurate statement, that your task was to prevent the Muslim fighters to enter the area, which is what you've testified, and that you were also supposed to take charge of the evacuation of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, we were supposed to take charge, yes, actually the unit itself, but did it take charge, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think I understand, sir. So we'll discuss what you yourself and the people around you were doing and I'll ask you some questions perhaps about what other members of the Jahorina contingent were doing and then -- and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, we're still on our way into Potocari on that -- that morning. Do you recall approximately what time of the morning you set off for Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: If I could recall properly, it was around 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you set off on foot or by vehicle to enter Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how did you proceed, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We had went into the formation group of -- of guys on the one side and group of guys on the other side. So-called tactical formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you yourself walking in the field, as it were, on the ground, or were you on a road of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We were on a road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was (redacted) among you as you entered Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I can't remember, to be quite honest with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: But I would say -- I would say that some of the leaders would be there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate for the Trial Chamber approximately how long it took you to reach the Dutch compound in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Probably two to three hours, I think, walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you hear any shooting or did you receive any fire, gunfire, as you approached Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber, sir, what you saw when you approached or when you actually came upon the UN compound there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: A lot of people. A lot of civilians there. They had been dressed as civilians. Lots of women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did you see them right at the Dutch compound itself in that factory building, or did you see them somewhere else, that mass of women and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: In the Dutch compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you also see Dutch soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you continue down that road a little bit further beyond the Dutch compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I can't recall it now, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber the condition of these civilians that you saw, both their physical condition, and if you can describe their emotional state if you were able to observe that as well, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was -- it was hot there and picture there was not really nice. Childrens were crying. People were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was your reaction, sir, personally to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I didn't like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you reached the base, when you reached this UN compound, did you see any other special police brigade, regular special police brigade, members or units there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I believe there were some, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there were any regular VRS, regular army units or soldiers at the Dutch compound when you arrived, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not inside the Dutch compound, no. Nobody was inside the compound, because Dutch soldiers would not allow nobody in -- in the Dutch compound at that stage. And later on in the day I did see few members of VRS as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any particular VRS units that stick out in your mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. I did -- I did see a few members from Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how was it that you knew that these people were with the Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: There -- there was insignia on their left shoulder on their uniforms on -- of wolf head.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how were you able to recognise these members of this regular special police brigade that you saw down at the Dutch compound when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: They -- they wore the similar insignia but different with -- with the White Eagle, so you can distinguished, and it's written down on that insignia what unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My last question before we take a break, sir, is can you describe what the special police brigade patch looked like? I think you started to a little bit, but if you could just describe what it looked like as best as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I can't remember now, that's the thing. It's 12 years down the track.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We understand, sir, and we'll move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, if we can take the break now. I think we've pretty much hit the mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, we are going to have a short break of 25 minutes, and then we'll resume soon after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good evening again to you, Witness. Are you with us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We're still in Potocari. I just asked you about whether you could remember the patches or emblems from the special police brigade. Do you recall what the uniforms of the regular special police brigade members looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. They are one-piece overall in camouflage colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the colours of the overalls were what, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Blue, green, red, black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: From memory I'm not sure in Potocari, but from memory I know there has been blue and green. At that stage I believe they were green.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you describe how you and your Jahorina recruits, fellow recruits, were deployed in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described a road. What road was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That was the road that we had been walking on to reach Potocari. I believe it was the main road that was leading to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did that main road run in front of the UN base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. How long did you remain in that location where you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Until late afternoon around 4.30, 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during that period of time what, if anything, did you see from your position with respect to the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I could not see civilians. I did see -- the only person that I had seen is the UN soldier on other side of the fence. I could not see civilians at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at any time did you see any buses in and around the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: At that time I can't remember seeing any buses in around the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On this day when you were in Potocari, do you recall ever seeing buses in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Do you remember -- do you remember what you told the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor back in 1995 about that topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not from 12 years down the track.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me direct you to the same witness statement, and it's at page 8. The ERN is 01499656, and the B/C/S, I believe, is also pages 7 through 8. Through the top of page 8, ending at 03074406. Sir, let me just direct your attention to the paragraph that starts: "I stayed there until the evening," and if you could just look at the first couple of sentences right above that paragraph. You discuss speaking with that Dutch officer -- or Dutch soldier, and then it says: "From there I could see buses and trucks on the road passing by. They arrived empty from the direction of Bratunac and they were crowded with people when they returned towards Bratunac." Let me ask you, sir, having read that portion of your statement, does that refresh your recollection, number one, about what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, that would --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry, does that refresh your recollection about what you told the OTP in 1995, first of all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that your memory, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, until I think you said about 16.30 did you leave that position for any reason until that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Until that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And why did you leave that position at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I was hungry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We went and we got some things to eat and tried to find some more water and trying to regroup because we have been there as a lost sheep. We didn't know what was happening, and plus we had been under the shock being scooped so fresh from Serbia. So we really, really didn't know what we're supposed to do next.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. During the course of that day did you see Mane in and around the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I haven't seen Mane in and around the UN compound at that point of time, but when I was giving the statement, I have seen the video. I have been shown the video where I have -- where I have recognised Mane on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll get to that a little bit later. What do you recall Mane's role being, if any, during this day at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: From -- from the video shown, it appeared to me that he was liaison officer of some sort with the gentleman from Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether at the time you had any information or that you learned any information or heard any information to indicate that Mane was acting in this role as a liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: There was a rumour that he was taking the role as a liaison officer. There was lots of rumour going in between the recruits.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, where you were, sir, were you able to observe any of the transportation of the civilians, either the grouping or the separation or the boarding of any of the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: During the course of this day, did you receive any information regarding who, if anyone, was taking part in that process of organising, separating, and boarding the civilians on those buses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, sir, before you give your answer. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just want to make one objection. I don't believe there is a foundation for this question, because if we look at the previous question, "During the course of this day, did you receive any information --" well, before this. "Were you able to observe any of the transportation of the civilian, either the grouping or the separation of the boarding." The answer was "No," of the witness. So this question that follows during the course did you receive any information was taking part in process, we need to know whether he has knowledge about this process going on, and if so then the follow-up question would be, Then how did you receive any such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I think one was predicated over there on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think that was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with his knowledge or otherwise of the events that you mentioned, that is this group or separation or -- or boarding of any of the buses, because you put them all in the alternative and not cumulatively. We could deal with that first and then you can put the second question to him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at any time during that day did you receive any information concerning what was actually happening to those civilians in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: After I have left that post where I had been, in talking with the other guys of the same unit in the same uniform, we could recognise each other in the same uniform. I have heard in a talk that actually there has been some separation, but I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally Mr. Thayer, while we are still on particular day, the witness hasn't been asked and he hasn't furnished us with any information as to the exact date when he first found himself in Potocari. If he would remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I've had some conversations with my friends on this topic. I'll put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what the date was that you arrived in Potocari? Do you recall the date that you entered Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say it was 13th of July, in between 13th and 15th. I'm not sure at this stage today in 2007, but it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, what is your recollection, sir, of the date that you left Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I believe thinking about it we perhaps left Jahorina on 13th, have came to destination probably 14th we have been in Potocari. If I could refresh my memory with the statement, but again you have to understand it is 12 years down the track, and I am trying to suppress all these memories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. One other thing for the record. Mr. Haynes for accused Pandurevic is now present in the courtroom. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Maybe we'll come back to the actual dates a little bit later. For now, though, I just want to work with what happened on these particular days, and let me just clarify. The first day we're talking about is the day you got the order to leave Jahorina and that you left Jahorina; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the second day is the day you entered Potocari; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, back to your conversation with your Jahorina colleague. You told us that he passed on to you information that there had been separations. Did he tell you whether he had any information about who was participating in those separations? What did he tell you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I cannot recall it, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just hang on a minute. Sir, I'd like to refer you to your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. It's at page 9. At the very top. It's ERN 01499657. And in the B/C/S that's at page 8, ERN 03074406. I just want to refer you to the section -- do you see where it says: "The evacuation was nearly over and from some conversations with soldiers forcibly brought from Serbia like myself who were in charge of overseeing the evacuation I learnt that 500 people had been evacuated from the UN compound and approximately 5.000 from Potocari"? First I want to ask you, sir, do you recall whether or not you actually said that to the investigators in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that a correct statement of what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next sentence is: "I heard that some soldiers and policemen had separated people before they boarded the buses. These people were taken to a house to be interviewed and after that put on buses and evacuated. I did not see anything and this was what was told to me." Do you recall saying that to the investigators in 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that accurate. That portion that I just read to you, is that true? Did that happen? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall seeing Dusko Jevic at any time during this day when you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Just briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was he doing, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: He was just standing up on the front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which house is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was the house and a photo was shown to me in -- when I had -- when I'd given the evidence, and that was the house. It was the "White House." I didn't pay too much attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that "White House", where in relation to the entrance to the UN compound is it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It's on the other side of the road, if I can recall it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the conversation that you had with your fellow Jahorina members, did they tell you what role, if any, Mane played in the separation of the men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't recall hearing anything of that role, if there was any.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you have any information or recollection as to where Mane was posted or operating during this day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I object. This question was already asked and answered. Before the break I believe that my colleague already asked whether he saw Mane on that day and whether he has any knowledge of what Mane did on this day, and the witness, I believe, said that he doesn't have any knowledge on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. -- we think Mr. Lazarevic's objection should be sustained. Please move to your next question, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you spend the night in Potocari or did you return to the school near Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We have returned to school near Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to returning, did you and your Jahorina recruits gather anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We did gather not immediately before the return but when we were around, you know, for food and water. We did gather around the house where the water was and we did see some women and children there and we gave them the food.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just talk about that for a second. What was the reaction, if any, that the civilians had to you when they saw you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: They were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did you leave Potocari in the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at any time prior to -- at any time prior to leaving on the buses were you mustered and reviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just take a moment and if I could just refer you again to your statement at page 9, ERN 01499657. And that is also on page 8, ERN 03074406, of the B/C/S version. I just direct your attention to the line that begins: "I left Potocari...." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether you did anything before you left, whether they were organised in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We had been organised as a formation in front of the compound and boarded the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately what time that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It would be probably around 9.00, 9.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you spend the night at that school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That brings us to the next day, sir. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what your assignment was that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: The following day we were supposed to have a day off, but in the afternoon we had been called up to relieve our colleagues, that they have been somewhere, and that was on a stretch of the road between Konjevic Polje and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you told what your colleagues had been doing on that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not at that point, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what did you do, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We had boarded the buses and we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you recall and describe the general location where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You indicated that this road ran between Kravica and Konjevic Polje. Had you ever --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to this area before that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Never in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine, sir. You indicated that you were replacing your fellow Jahorina members. Did you see any members of the regular special police or any other military units there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my memory there was -- we had seen few guys from the special police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether there was any attempt to communicate with any Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. There had been calls on a megaphone to come down and they're going to be shipped away and exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall to which unit the person who was doing that belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my memory, it was regular special police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And let me just ask you again, sir, because I think I asked you a compound question before and I apologise. Do you recall seeing any regular army units or soldiers in this location when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Where, in school or where? Can you clarify the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When you arrived at this area that you described as

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I haven't seen to my knowledge, to my memory, any members of military at that stage then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And physically would you please describe for the Trial Chamber how exactly you and your Jahorina recruits were deployed along that road? How many and what distances approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was -- it was two approximately every 50 to 100 metres again, but it was in pairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And could you see your fellow recruits to your left and your right from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: On the road, yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you were deployed to the road, what was your assignment while you were on that road? To do what, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Just to be on the road and perhaps collect any -- anybody that comes down, or to prevent any forcible passing through from -- from the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say perhaps to collect people that were coming down, can you be more precise about what you're talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: If was anybody coming down to surrender, our task was perhaps to take them and -- and just pass them on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Was that perhaps your assignment or was that in fact your assignment while you were on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We hadn't been debriefed about assignments as such, and I don't recall being given any tasks as such. We just have been told that we need to be there on a stretch of the road. If anybody surrenders, alert your authorities so you can pass the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, sir, do you have any recollection of who passed on those instructions to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Those instructions would have been passed by the command -- by the platoon leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, that -- that actual day when you first arrived to this location (redacted) and when you were deployed, did you personally take part in any surrender by any Muslims that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Nobody did surrender to me and my colleague directly. Whoever was surrendering, there was about 100, 150 metres away from us, uphill there was a small road coming from the mountains, and whoever was coming from the mountain was going along those -- along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: And they would go to -- to the other guys. And then the other guys would get the men and -- and call for -- for whoever is going to come -- come to pick them up and just sit them and -- and guard them for the prisoners to be picked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say other guys, sir, are you referring to your fellow Jahorina -- your fellow Jahorina members, the -- the regular special police brigade members, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Along the stretch of the road to my knowledge from what I've seen we have been from fellow Jahorina, and if anybody would surrender at that point in time to that stretch of road, it could be surrendering to Jahorina guys. And then they would be calling in to their -- like whoever is on the top of them, informing them that actually we have a prisoner or somebody has got a prisoner, and then the vehicle would show up and pick them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you just a question about the communications. How were people communicating with each other amongst yourselves, your Jahorina colleagues, and the superior officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Well, all depends how high you're going superior officers in between us. We're just talking. We didn't have any other mean of communications. And it was above us, the guys, they had hand-held two-way radios.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what level soldier or special police member had those two-way radios?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my recollection the two-way radio was given to these guys that -- Jahorina members who were in charge of these smaller units to report to their commanding officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when -- when you say Jahorina members, do you recall whether any of the recruits like yourself had these two-way radios, or were the only people with two-way radios regular special police members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Some of the members of Jahorina, very few, had these two-way radios.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And what do you recall the regular special police brigade members doing during this day when people were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: They were just calling them down, to my knowledge. They were calling them down.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when these buses arrived to take the prisoners away, were the prisoners escorted on these buses? Were they guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I would say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall whether it was Jahorina members guarding them or regular special police brigade members or someone else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: On the buses -- on the buses definitely not Jahorina members. And I'm not sure about the regular special police members and -- and the army, I'm not sure about that, but to my recollection on these buses Jahorina members were not on. Jahorina members were going with the other vehicles later on. You know, day or two down the track.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the coordination and communication, if any, between the Jahorina recruits like yourself and the special police brigade, the regular special police brigade members, who were there in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't recall any direct communication. I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, did you have an understanding based on any information that you received what the communication or coordination was between the Jahorina members and the regular special police brigade members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's basically the same question that was posed a second ago. The witness, I believe, clearly answered that he has -- he doesn't recall any direct communication between these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just interpreted his answer to mean personal. That's why I went to the general in my follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's still the same thing, but if you can bring out the difference between the previous question and this one, explain it, in other words, to the witness, then you may put the question, but you need to rephrase it of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
