utterances.text: Sir, did you become aware at any time during this day as to whether there was any communication or coordination of any kind between the regular Jahorina members and the regular -- I'm sorry, the Jahorina recruits like yourself and the regular special police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my knowledge I didn't know that there was any direct communication. What was more a feeling is that we were like sheep there. We didn't know what to do. So when we had been posted somewhere, we stood there without asking many questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall who would be consulted if you did have questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: If I did have a question I would have to go through the Jahorina member who had the two-way radio and ask the question or raise an issue, and he would call up whomever he needs to call up to resolve the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir. Do you remember what you said on this issue in your deposition taken in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I showed you a portion of that transcript, do you think that might help refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me direct you to page 12 of the English, lines 23 to 32. That's ERN 01499695 in the English and page 10 of the B/C/S at 03074530, the third question and answer on that page. Do you see the question: "How was it when the prisoners were collected that you were able to notify somebody that they needed to be picked up?" And your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see the answer, "There was a group of the normal regular police force and they had such device and somebody would run to them and tell, like, we have a few prisoners"? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall saying that during the deposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that an accurate statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It would be, is he.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the following question: "Where was the contingent of regular special police located?" And your answer is, "A bit further up, maybe half a K."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yeah half a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just a clarification. When you refer to having such a device what are you talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Two-way radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So you're referring to contacting the regular special police brigade officers via two-way radio; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you some questions about another series of events. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what, if anything, you recall that stands out in your mind happening later that day, that same day that you arrived (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) And very, very late in the afternoon, early, early evening, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: And on which the reaction was, "Really? Are you crazy? What are you saying?" (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Thayer, something that needs some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand Mr. President's question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir on this -- on this first day when you were deployed along the road, did you begin hearing about any (redacted) executions which occurred in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not in the first day but one or two days down the track, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber what you heard and from whom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I heard it from the fellow recruit that actually has been in one of the escorts with the smaller vehicle of some of the prisoners to a store facility in Kravica, that actually that has been something.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to a store facility, what kind of facility or structure are you talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: A warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did this fellow Jahorina member tell you happened at this warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: These prisoners that we are supposed to be sent and exchanged to Tuzla actually have been executed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was this fellow recruit's reaction to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: He was cursing. He could not believe what is happening, because we have had far too many shocks in a short distance, in short period of time that we have been there and we just could not believe that that is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you who was executing these prisoners, what unit the killers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: He did mention that they did belong to a regular special police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall approximately how many days you spent deployed along this stretch of road while the Muslims were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my knowledge and to my recollection around five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you also receive at some point a new assignment that had to do with this road that you were posted on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no. And those five days that we have been on a stretch of road I cannot recall any new assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall being tasked along with some regular VRS units to sweep the terrain anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, but that was after we had been withdrawn from the stretch of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe approximately how long after you had withdrawn from that stretch of the road you were given this new assignment, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: When we have been retrieved from the stretch of the road I believe we had been given half of the day off or even whole day off and then we would sweep the terrain with -- with military force the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you just describe personally what you did during this sweep operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Personally we had every person to my left and my right every probably two to three metres and walking along the bushes and the trees and trying to find any survivors or prisoners or anything. Just to sweep the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall the approximate location in which you performed this sweep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No, sir, it was a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall in relation to Kravica where you were performing this sweep or in relation to Konjevic Polje? And if you can't remember, that's fine, I'll move on, but I just want to see what your recollection is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I really cannot recollect, but my -- I believe that it was from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you encounter any Muslims during this sweep, whether they were alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We did. We did encounter a few dead bodies, and not close to me. It was a few left like pocket of resistance that actually was higher up in the mountain that actually regular police force was called in to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you see or did you become aware of any Muslims surrendering during this sweep operation, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not to me, but when we came down I did see few people did surrender, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say a few people, can you describe the size of this group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Probably around, I don't know, 10 to 20. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what you told the investigators from the OTP during your interview in 1995 on this topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Would you mind if I had a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll give you the site. Hold on one second, please. If you turn -- sir, if you turn to page 14 of your OTP witness statement. In the English that's ERN 01499662. And in the B/C/S I believe that's page 12, ERN 03074410. And I just draw your attention to the second paragraph headed "Sometime later."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see where it says: "While you were on the road we saw the military unit coming downhill with a group of about 100 to 150 prisoners"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- do you recall saying that to the investigators at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and this was in referral to the army people, and I did -- I did say -- just on this note, I did say that my estimate might not be accurate, because I don't think that my estimate would be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you. As you sit here now, what is your best recollection of how many prisoners this group of army soldiers came down the hill with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It definitely would be two busloads, and that would be probably in the vicinity of 100 to 150, but I just wanted to make sure that you don't take me that it was 100 or 150, because my estimates are not that great with numbers and age.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. And do you know where these prisoners were taken and by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: They have been boarded on buses and taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was this by the army or by the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I cannot recall that, because I believe that some of the drivers I've seen have been civilians, and it's difficult to differentiate who's who when everybody is wearing camouflage uniform, and you can differentiate between camouflage uniform and civilian clothes, and it's very hard to make a judgement when you had whole day walking through the woods on a -- on a hot day, very tired, very stressed out. It's very, very difficult to -- to make correct observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. And if I may, let me just go back to the time when you were deployed along that road from Kravica to Konjevic Polje and were waiting for prisoners and being on the lookout for prisoners surrendering. Do you recall whether you during that period of time, any time while you were posted there during that five days as you recall the number of days, do you recall whether you personally took any Muslim who surrendered into custody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not myself. Myself and my partner, we did have one attempt of surrendering, and we just waved the person to go away. We just told him to go -- just waved to go away. We didn't want to take them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you observe any Muslims surrendering during that five days in your vicinity, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It was one particular surrendering of one Muslim fighter or civilian or how you call it that actually is in my memory. The guy came in, probably around 150 to 200 metres uphill, up-road, surrendering to a person, recruit from Jahorina, and on the point of surrendering he had handmade grenade that actually he has throw down on this person, and that Muslim that has been surrendering has been shot in self-defense. But the person, we have been told later that actually the person, the Jahorina recruit was severely disabled with that incident. He was alive but severely disabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, other than the first day on which you arrived (redacted) (redacted), after that first day whether or not you personally saw any Muslim surrendering, can you estimate for the Trial Chamber based on what you were hearing how many Muslims were surrendering on a given day while you were posted there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: On a given day when we were posted there, on the first day there was a lot of people there before we arrived. On our arrival it was a lot of people, but everyday it was very few, not much, not many, and going into the third, fourth, and fifth day it was basically nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, back to this -- the sweep operation. How many days did you spend doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where were you deployed next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I believe we went back to Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say, sir, just to move things along, that after that you were deployed in the Manjaca area and elsewhere through the fall of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct, yes, but not through Jahorina unit. In -- through Jahorina unit after we had been on Potocari and after mission, we have been sent to guard the lines on a nearby hill, but with Manjaca that was afterwards, after Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you were -- you were made part of a -- of a different brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how your military service came to an end? Again without, if you can, identifying yourself in any way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: After we went on Manjaca and when we came back to the base

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I just have a little bit more time that I want to spend with you, and I'd like to show you some brief video clips. I think you've already described them or referred to them, and with any luck you'll be able to see them through the transmission.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence, I just want to verify. Mr. President, for the record we will be reviewing a segment from the trial video, Exhibit number P02047. The -- the first segment will run from 2 hours 25 minutes and 55.00 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, are you receiving the video feed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We've paused for the record at 2:26:18:3. Do you recognise anyone in this video still?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay. I don't know the gentleman standing there with the bullet-proof vest, but that person is more than likely a person that has been brought from Serbia in Jahorina camp with us. And the gentleman on our right-hand side, by the appearance I would say he is a UN soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what makes you say that you believe that the other person without the blue beret was a Jahorina recruit like yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Same bullet-proof vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. We're going to continue to run the video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've seen this video clip before. We're pausing at 2:26 -- bear with us. We're having technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I apologise. I cannot see the witness, the image of the video. I don't have the image of the witness from (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, but that's how it has to be. Whenever we are playing a video, then automatically you get a blank screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise then for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think you might need a redaction there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. It's Mr. Lazarevic [inaudible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm being advised by the court reporter that she just needs the page and line citation for the redaction again. It wasn't picked up. It wasn't audible for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The page is page 62 of our transcript, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've paused at 2:26:27:4. Having viewed this video clip previously and seen it again now, do you recognise any one in this video still.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: The gentleman and the left is the gentleman that disguised himself by the name Mane.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir. We are going to show you a second video clip that will run for approximately three and a half minutes. And for the record, this will begin at 2:45:37.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've just reviewed a video clip shot from a car on this road. We have paused at 2:47:23:1. First I ask you whether you were able to observe any soldiers being deployed along that stretch of the road on this video clip.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how does that correspond to your recollection of how you and your fellow Jahorina members were deployed while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That was us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, showing you this particular video still at the time I've mentioned. Do you recognise what unit this individual depicted in it belongs to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That gentleman was from Jahorina, but from which particular unit I don't recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. We'll just continue running for another minute or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've stopped at 2:47:52:6. Do you recognise to which unit the individual in this video still belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That gentleman did belong to Jahorina unit as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of either of these two men as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, just a couple of more questions for you. Sir, are you aware of any investigation being initiated by the Republika Srpska special police brigade following deployment of the forces including your forces to Potocari and the road that you described in July of 1995? Are you aware of any investigation being initiated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Investigation, you mean of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Of any activities by the Special Police Brigade or by your Jahorina unit. Are you aware of any investigation being initiated by the RS special police following your deployment there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I was too low to had such a knowledge of anything like that. Even if it was initiated, which I'm not aware of, I would definitely not heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Well, let me ask you, did Dusko Jevic or Mane or any other officer from the Jahorina training centre ask you for a report concerning the actions of you and your fellow colleagues or regular special police members concerning your activities in Potocari and along that road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What were you told at the time, sir, would happen to you, if anything, if you ever spoke about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: We would end up in The Hague being tried for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you ever threatened in any way concerning your personal safety if you ever spoke about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I don't recall any direct threats, but we have been told that actually we might be -- we will be picked up and get prosecuted by The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who told you that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: To my recollection that gentleman would have been Dusko Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when did he tell you that, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: It would have been -- I don't remember to pinpoint the accuracy, but it would have been on the end of all events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- one question while you check whatever you're checking, Mr. Thayer. Witness, when according to you this Dusko Jevic gave you this warning or threat, were you alone at the time with him or were there others present --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I'm sorry to interrupt, but no. We had all been said in group, in the various group that at the time it was believed in 1995 that Hague is only to be tried to Serbs and -- and we've been there. We will be tried on Hague if we ever spoke about anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just one follow-up question. Do you remember what you said in your deposition about any threats that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Would you mind if I look up and refresh my memory?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll refer you to page 35, line 23 in the English. And I believe that's page 30, ERN 03074550 of the B/C/S and the ERN on the English is 01499718. The question was put to you: "Do you recall being threatened with death if you ever told anybody what you had seen..." Do you see that question, sir? I know this isn't easy, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: This question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Sorry to interrupt you, but we have an objection. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness should read the whole paragraph because frankly from what comes from following lines it's basically the same that he said right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We don't have -- thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. We don't have a copy of the statement, so we take your word for it, and I suggest the witness to follow the advice of -- or suggestion of Mr. Lazarevic and read the entire paragraph and then perhaps he can proceed to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Do you recall being threatened with death if you ever told anybody that you had seen or what you have to be -- or that you would have to be tried before a criminal tribunal for war crimes?" Answer: "Yes." "Who would threaten in that manner?" "If everybody, all superior officers, they used to come around and tell us, like, if you go and talk about anything about war, about here, you're going to end up in The Hague. You like struck in Bosnia. You have nowhere to go. If you go they're going to grab you. They're going to trial you."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you remember giving that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes. And I did give correct answer yes, we have been threatened that we have -- that we going to be prosecuted in The Hague but not directly death threats, because there is -- I believe there are two questions in this question, and I did answer this question with yes. Not direct life threats but it was a threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let me refer you to another statement that you gave even before your statement to the OTP in December of 1995. This is the statement to the UNHCR. In English it's 01499641, paragraph 19. And in the B/C/S it's page 3, also paragraph 19, 03074666.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a matter of clarification whether we are going to consider it to be a witness statement or just notes taken from the interview of the witness, because I would really like to be fair toward witness and I believe that my colleague also have same intent. This was not written by the witness. This is sort of notes from the statements that witness gave to -- to officials of UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer can answer that. We cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my submission is that this is a very, very detailed recordation by somebody that interviewed this witness, and I can clarify the basis for this document in a question for the witness and then ask him one question and we'll be concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The whole thing boils down to the following: Is that other statement, the way you've described or referred to it, is it a collection of notes taken during an interview with the witness or is it a verbatim transcript of a recording of an interview with the witness by someone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say it's in between. It's a very detailed narrative account based on the interview or interviews that he had with the UNHCR in much the same way that a witness statement is recorded by the investigator. Although I don't think this was signed by the -- by the witness, it is a document that is drawn up based on obviously whatever notes were taken during the course of the interviews and turned into a very detailed report, as it were. I would refer to it as a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. I think for the time being you may proceed, and then we regulate your questions if necessary, and if Mr. Lazarevic draws our attention to any problem that he envisages. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 19, and you were referred to in this document simply by some initials, "IC," do you see where it says, "'IC' was threatened of death if he told anyone what he saw and that if he did so he would have been tried by a tribunal for war crimes"? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Before -- yes, I can see that, but before we continue discussing this statement given in UNHCR, I just would like to make a point that I did raise a lot of discrepancy in this statement simply because interpreter was Macedonian with a poor command of Serbian language, and I did raise lots of discrepancy in this statement, and I don't agree with -- with some of the things in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, my final question to you is simple, sir. Do you agree or disagree with the statement made here in this document that you were threatened with death if you ever spoke about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I disagree that I had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... that--

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- threatened with death.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe he disagreed and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- also made an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is being corrected now, Mr. Lazarevic. So thank you Mr. Thayer, and thank you, Witness, for your cooperation. We need to have a break now. We'll have a 25-minute break, but before we do so, let me see, is there a problem? Does any one of the accused have a problem? No. All right. We'll have -- if you have a problem, speak up. Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's first have a revised estimate of the anticipated cross-examinations. The Pandurevic, Gvero, and Nikolic teams have indicated that they don't wish to cross-examine this witness. Is that still the position? Okay. Mr. Zivanovic for --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not cross-examine this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Nothing. All right. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. So basically that leaves you, Mr. Lazarevic. Take your time, and I understand that the witness is available also tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Yaiza.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [] Well, in fact, we're wanting to know if we will need to be here tomorrow because we need to organise here since -- yeah, wanting to have -- to make some arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In fact, my next --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [] [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. MAGISTRATE (redacted): [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I couldn't hear Magistrate (redacted) MAGISTRATE (redacted): Tomorrow it [Realtime transcript read in error "does"] doesn't pose a difficulty, Mr. President, but if it goes beyond tomorrow, we'll have to make arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you. I'm sure of that and I appreciate that, Magistrate. My next question is, Mr. Lazarevic, is how long do you anticipate your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I will be able to complete my cross-examination today. I believe I will have to stick to my estimation, my previous estimation of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your estimation was one hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's start. So tomorrow we will need roughly one hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were discussing whether it was at all possible to proceed beyond quarter to 2.00, but it seems that logistically that will be difficult because another -- another trial needs to start at quarter past 2.00 and they have one witness that they need to finish today. So -- yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to confuse matters but I think what the learned Magistrate said, that it doesn't prove a difficulty tomorrow and it's been transcribed wrongly. I think that's what he said, and unfortunately, our transcript says the complete opposite. Your Honour might want to confirm with the learned Magistrate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Josse. I have the same impression. I didn't compare what I heard with what the transcript says, but I just heard that Magistrate (redacted) saying that he needs to know so that they make the necessary arrangements in any case. Is that correct, Magistrate? MAGISTRATE (redacted): Mr. President, tomorrow poses no difficulty whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. MAGISTRATE (redacted): It only poses a difficulty if it goes beyond the six hours we've set aside tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. That's very clear. Thank you. And we won't need all the time that has been allotted in any case, there being no further cross-examinations except for the Borovcanin Defence team. Mr. Lazarevic, please go ahead with your cross-examination, and could you introduce yourself to the witness and to Magistrate (redacted), please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Magistrate (redacted). My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and today together with my colleagues here I appear for Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin. Witness, in this examination I will address you as witness or sir without mentioning your name, and the only reason for that is to protect your identity. Please do not misunderstand me as trying to humiliate you in any way or to offend you. This is purely for purposes of protecting your identity. Do you accept is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we start then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, first of all I would like to identify, because I believe there has been some confusion created in the course of examination-in-chief. All your statements that you have given so far related to the events in Srebrenica. The first one, I believe, was given in Skopje from the 14th through the 18th of -- or through the 17th of November, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have had occasion recently to review again this document. I don't know if I should call it a proper statement. You have seen it in the course of examination-in-chief or prior to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: When? When was that? When are you referring to? Which time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the fact that this document has just been shown to you during the examination-in-chief conducted by my learned friend from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just to try to establish the status of that document, when you reviewed it, and you are free to look at it again, is that a document written in the first-person singular, as if you personally wrote it as a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: I did not wrote it as a statement. I was talking to the gentleman in UNHCR through the interpreter which is of different origin and different language than Serbian, and that person did have difficulty grasping all the meaning of Serbian language, and my command of English was not very well, so I couldn't talk directly to the gentleman that I was speaking to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record before you proceed, Mr. Lazarevic, on line 18 of page -- on page 73 you see November 1995 there. It should be December 1995, I suppose. Do you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it should read November, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then the information that we were given -- it's a witness statement here. The date is 12/12/1995. Mr. Thayer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, our understanding was that that statement was finalised on December 12th, and part of that may be from the fax line which we see at the top of that statement. But frankly I don't have the cover sheet or -- or the -- any other documentation that indicates when precisely this UNHCR series of interviews were conducted. We know that it was before December 12th. And if you look at paragraph 45 of the document it refers to the 14th, 15th, and 17th of November, but we don't know when it was actually finalised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then Mr. Lazarevic seems to be right and we can proceed accordingly. Mr. Lazarevic. Thank you, Mr. Thayer, and thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I thank my learned friend for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that you have looked at this document, let us clear up one thing. You never signed this document to confirm the veracity of its contents, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After that you met with the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY from the 14th through the 18th December 1995, and on that occasion your written statement was compiled and it has been extensively used during your examination. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more thing. According to my records, on the 24th of July, 2002, you gave another statement in your country of residence before a magistrate. Is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we have identified these three statements, have you given any other statements before any other court, state authority, or any other body in charge of investigation of any kind other than the three I have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the statements that you have given, the three that I have mentioned, that is, you told the truth to the best of your recollection as far as these events are concerned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move on to the substance of your testimony as we heard it today. It was new to me because it was not in any of your statements, but you answered to one of the Prosecutor's question saying you did not do your military service in the former socialist federal Republic of Yugoslavia before June 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: What I meant with that answer, I was not associated with the war happening in Bosnia, but I did do compulsory conscription (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That clears up my confusion, because I had understood previously that you had never been in the army at all. So you did serve the 12 or 13 months, whatever it was at the time, of compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can we just go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are in open session, Witness and Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thus the number that you have given us as far as I can understand is an approximation. You are not a hundred per cent sure about the number of the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In this regard I would like to show you another document which is 4D00119.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would like to just verify with our legal officer whether she -- I'm sure that she doesn't have a hard copy of this document. We are requested to provide all hard copies of the documents that we intend to use during cross-examination seven days ago, and in our review we found this document only two days ago. I gave a copy of the document to the Prosecution. It is in e-court, but I don't believe that the hard copy of this document is available to the witness right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that, but I think we can upload it if it is in e-court and show it to the witness just the same. Can you verify that, please? Is this the document you had in mind, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we can proceed, assuming that the witness can see it. We will zoom in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will zoom in as required, as we go along, but the important thing is you are receiving at least the image of this document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the documents but they are fairly blurry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine that, but we will be zooming in the -- on the relevant parts, so don't worry about it. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, maybe it won't be that important for you to see the document clearly because I'm just going to read the relevant portion of it. The document was sent by the deputy minister of the interior of Republika Srpska on the 23rd of June, 1995, to the President of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic. In the first paragraph of this document it reads as follows: "With regard to your document, confidential number 01-1118-3/95, dated 22nd June, 1995, we hereby inform you that by 1000 hours on 23 June 1995 our collection centres in Janja and Zvornik have handed over to the VRS armed forces a total of 1.586 conscripts delivered by MUP Serbia. Of this number, 149 conscripts were handed over to the MUP staff on Mount Jahorina." Witness, I assume that you have not had an occasion to see this document before. However, now that I have read the relevant portion of it to you, you see that according to this document 149 men were sent to Jahorina at the time. Would you say that perhaps this number is a better reflection of the number of people who found themselves on Mount Jahorina at the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: That could be the case. As I have indicated before, my number estimates are not that great.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will no longer need this document. Based on the statements you provided to the UNHCR, I can tell that you spoke about your position, about the units that you joined, and you said there, if your words were transcribed correctly, about that unit was that that unit should have been part of the reserve force of the army of Republika Srpska. First of all, can you tell me whether you adhere by the position that your unit was a reserve unit of the army of Republika Srpska? And if you do adhere by that and if that is still your position, can you tell us what would be the basis of your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-100.
utterances.text: Okay. When we got to Janja, we have been asked where -- like we have had some sort of choice where we would like to go, and on a question what is the choice, we have been told that the choice is in between police and army. On further question what would the police do, we have been told it's going to be a duty of police reserve guarding the consuls, guarding the premises, not involving in a combat situation, on which I have asked to go that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understood your answer very well. However, the statement says that your unit was part of the reserve forces of the VRS, but I believe that your answer that you have just given us provides enough clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours there are two more minutes to go and I am now moving to a completely different topic, so maybe it would be useful to adjourn for today at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. We'll do so. Witness, our time is up. We are stopping here for today. We will continue tomorrow starting at the same time as today. (redacted) (redacted). And I also wish to thank you, Magistrate (redacted), and your assistant, for cooperating in this, for your patience. We will see you again tomorrow morning, tomorrow evening or afternoon in your case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
